newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia govt reforms insurance firms tax rules.
newsitem.headline: Australia govt reforms insurance firms tax rules.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello on Tuesday announced changes to tax assessments for life insurance companies to iron out distorted tax payments.
Tax exemptions for annuity policies would now be based on average liabilities over the fiscal year.
Similar averaging would be applied in calculating income and capital gains tax across all business of a life insurance company, Costello said in a statement.
Currently, calculations were based on liabilities at the end of the fiscal year.

"However, this causes distortions if the proportion of calculated liabilities...at the end of the income year does not reflect the respective proportions of calculated liabilities...during the income year," Costello said.

"The use of average calculated liabilities produces a better reflection of the amount of income that belongs to each of the classes of policy held by a life insurance company and overcomes the distortions."
Calculation details would be developed in consultation with the industry.
Costello said the reforms would operate from today and would generally begin in the 1997/98 fiscal year.
However, the new system would be used in 1996/97 if there was a "significant" variation in calculated liabilities for the remainder of the fiscal year.
Tax officials were not available to say what would be regarded as a significant variation, or to give further details.
